GeneratedSpec.description:
How generated code is told apart: the same shape in a project, in a
plugin manifest and in anything `extends` brings; both lists merge as the
union. Whether generated code is a subject is not said here: a decision's
`scope.generated` and a rule's `generated` say that.

files.description:
Patterns of project-relative paths that are generated code: the syntax
and the matcher of `ignores`.

markers.description:
Regular expressions searched in the comments at the head of a file (the
ones before its first symbol), delimiters included, whatever its
language: a file one of them matches is generated code.

Metadata.description:
Who a resource is. Identity is `name`; grouping is by label, never by
where the document is stored.

annotations.description: Free notes; never used to select.

uid.description:
Identity that outlives the name: a UUID v4 assigned once, never derived
from the name (Kubernetes `metadata.uid`). Renaming a resource keeps it.

PluginSpec.description:
The spec of the `Plugin` kind: how to start a plugin process, and what the
plugin provides.

catalog.description:
Directory of the plugin's decision catalog, relative to the manifest
directory: the packs the plugin provides, read without starting the
process.

generated.description:
How the plugin's ecosystem marks its generated code: the same key,
shape and merge as the project's `generated`.

ignores.description:
The files the plugin's toolchain leaves out of a project: the same
key, syntax and meaning as the project's `ignores` (gitignore
patterns, rooted at the project), and merged the same way, before the
project's own.

runtime.description:
How to start the plugin's process; a bundled plugin, which the binary
compiles in, has none.

Provides.description:
What a plugin contributes, declared so that tools can list it without
starting the process. Each list is checked against what the process
reports when it starts.

Runtime.description: How a plugin process is started.

command.description:
Executable. A relative path with a separator is resolved against the
manifest directory; a bare name is looked up on `PATH`.
